reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: Verified against code at beacon_chain/networking/eth2_network.nim:2211-2236. The peerPingerHeartbeat function uses a fixed 30-minute timer (MetadataRequestFrequency) with no fork-aware acceleration. 01e spec (01e_PARTIAL_MANUAL_15_109_190_216.json, lines 36-50) explicitly requires: 'After a protocol upgrade or fork transition, all peer metadata fields that are semantically redefined by the new protocol version (e.g., custody_group_count becoming meaningful at Fulu) must be refreshed from each connected peer within a bounded time.' The code violates this by allowing up to 30 minutes of stale metadata. An attacker can exploit this timing window at Fulu fork activation: peers connected before fork retain custody_group_count=0, causing matchIntersection (request_manager.nim:374-384) to compute zero overlap, blocking data column sync requests. Severity remains Medium per bug bounty scope: affects data availability during critical fork transition window, meeting >5% network impact threshold for fork-synchronous issues.
reviewed_items.spec_reference: 01e requirement: 'After a protocol upgrade or fork transition, all peer metadata fields that are semantically redefined by the new protocol version must be refreshed within a bounded time. Stale pre-transition default values must not be used for post-transition decisions.'
